claim.quote: We present measurements of nu_mu disappearance in K2K, the KEK to Kamioka long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment. ... The probability that the observations are explained by the expectation for no neutrino oscillation is 0.0015% (4.3sigma).

date.note: arXiv submission June 2006; published as Phys. Rev. D 74, 072003 (2006).

key_value_text.note: key_value (Quantity) is left null: the ontology's Quantity unit/dimension table has no unit for a mass-squared splitting (eV^2); the value is instead carried here as free text with a verbatim quote, per section 3.12 (key_value_text).
key_value_text.quote: a best-fit value of 2.8 x 10^{-3} eV^2
key_value_text.value: Best fit Delta m^2 = 2.8 x 10^-3 eV^2 (allowed range 1.9-3.5 x 10^-3 eV^2 at 90% CL, maximal mixing); 112 beam-originated neutrino events observed at Super-Kamiokande vs. 158.1(+9.2/-8.6) expected without oscillation.

name: K2K measurement of muon-neutrino disappearance

summary.plain: K2K sent a beam of neutrinos 250 km underground from KEK to Super-Kamiokande and found fewer of them arrived than expected - and with the wrong energies - confirming with a controlled, human-made beam what Super-Kamiokande had already seen in natural atmospheric neutrinos.
summary.technical: 112 observed vs. 158.1(+9.2/-8.6) expected beam-originated events in the SK fiducial volume, plus a distorted energy spectrum in 58 single-ring muon-like events; no-oscillation hypothesis excluded at 4.3 sigma; two-flavour fit gives Delta m^2 in [1.9,3.5]e-3 eV^2 (90% CL), best fit 2.8e-3 eV^2.

title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation by the K2K Experiment
why_it_matters: First confirmation of neutrino oscillation using an artificial, well-characterised accelerator beam rather than natural atmospheric or solar neutrinos, validating the interpretation of the atmospheric-neutrino anomaly and establishing the long-baseline accelerator method used ever since (K2K, MINOS, T2K, NOvA, DUNE).
